issues.legal_issue: A claim of discriminatory land allotment is not established when the alleged comparator and the details of the different allotment are not specifically pleaded, and the claim was not shown to have been raised before the deciding judge.
material_facts: The appellant alleged generally that similarly situated institutions had received land allotments, but did not identify the comparator or provide details of its allotment in the writ petition.
The appellant did not substantiate its assertion that discriminatory treatment had been raised before the Single Judge, and it did not seek review of that judge’s decision.
A different educational society had received a four-acre allotment before the challenged policy decision, but no four-acre allotment after that decision was shown.
issues.conclusion: The High Court committed no error in rejecting the claim, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: A judge’s record must be accepted as correct. Where a party says an argument was raised but not addressed, it may seek review; an unsupported assertion in an appeal does not establish that the argument was made. A discrimination claim must identify the allegedly comparable treatment with sufficient specificity to permit a response.

predicates.appeal_from_writ_dismissal: The party appealed after a court dismissed its petition challenging an administrative decision.
predicates.discrimination_claim_lacks_comparator_de: The party alleged unequal treatment but did not specify the comparator and the relevant details of that comparator’s treatment.
predicates.claim_not_shown_raised_before_deciding_j: The party did not substantiate that it had raised the discrimination argument before the judge who first decided the petition.
predicates.no_review_sought: The party did not ask the first-instance judge to review the decision for failing to address the alleged argument.

issues.definition: When a party appeals the dismissal of a petition and its discrimination claim lacks comparator details, the claim is rejected if it was not shown to have been raised before the deciding judge or no review was sought.

issues.legal_issue: A challenge to a policy limiting school land allotments was not a basis to disturb the High Court’s decision where the official records showed that the Central Government considered and approved the policy’s implementation.
material_facts: The Master Plan provided for four acres of land for a secondary school, while the development authority adopted a policy of allotting only two acres.
The High Court found that official Central Government records showed that the authority’s recommendations had been considered and approved for implementation.
The High Court found that land rates were determined by the Central Government, and the Supreme Court accepted those findings and declined to take a different view.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court declined to disturb the High Court’s rejection of the challenge, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court accepted the High Court’s findings based on the official records that the Central Government had considered and approved implementation of the recommendations and had determined the land rates; it therefore rejected the contention that there had been excessive delegation or a basis to take a different view. No statute or earlier case was cited for this determination.

predicates.appeal_from_writ_dismissal: The party appealed after a court dismissed its petition challenging an administrative decision.
predicates.policy_challenge_to_reduced_school_land_: The party challenged a policy that provided less land for a school than the planning document specified.
predicates.central_government_considered_and_approv: The Central Government considered the relevant recommendations and approved their implementation.
predicates.official_records_support_high_court_find: Official records reviewed by the High Court supported its findings about the government’s consideration and approval.

issues.definition: When an appeal from dismissal of a petition challenges a policy reducing school land allotments, the challenge is rejected if the Central Government approved implementation and official records support the High Court’s findings.
